_batch.cross_item_tell: Options are sorted ascending in every item and my key is an EXTREME option (A or D) on 24 of 32 (A 12: P2,P3,P4,P10,Q2,Q5,Q6,Q9,R5,R6,R8,R9; D 12: P6,P7,P8,P9,Q4,Q7,Q8,Q10,R2,R3,R4,R7; B 6; C 2). "Always pick an extreme" scores 75% vs 50% for interior; picking A alone or D alone scores 37.5% vs 25%. No answer-value recipe recurs that I can name without the distractor paths; whole batch shares one method (evaluate at both interval endpoints, intersect), so the template pairs listed are tight clusters within a single family. Stage 2 addition: the distractor recipe recurs across almost every item - one is "assumes the slope (or relative slope) has one sign only", one is "checks only one endpoint / one boundary", and many have "difference instead of sum" or "counts integer k instead of the target". The one-sign distractor always yields a sub-interval, so in sum/range items it never brackets the key; this does not by itself identify the key, but a student who knows the recipe can strike the one-sign option on sight in most items.
